items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: The first big band I played with... was Les Hite. I played in that band and during the time I was in that band Dizzy Gillespie also joined it

ctx.x: How about your first big band experience? You’ve played in so many big bands.

The first big band I played with, a name orchestra, was Les Hite. I played in that band and during the time I was in that band Dizzy Gillespie also joined it, Britt Woodman was the first trombone player, and Gerald Wiggins, Britt Woodman and his brother Coney, who was our pianist, were drafted at the same time. And Gerald Wiggins joined the band. He was in the band at the time Dizzy Gillespie was in the band for a short time.
Did you get to do some traveling at that point, around the country, did you travel?

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Dizzy Gillespie played in that band... Dizzy joined the band... He was a joy to be with... I’m sitting there trying to stop laughing, so I can play, and Dizzy’s sitting there

ctx.x: Who was he playing with? What kinds of bands was he playing with?

He played with dance bands in Philadelphia, and nightclubs. He played with one band, Frankie Fairfax, who was a trombonist, and Dizzy Gillespie played in that band. I think that’s when they called him – he got the nickname Dizzy, because Dizzy was always a prankster. He was always doing little funny things. My father, he’s older. Let’s see. My father’s about 20 years older than Dizzy. Yeah. So most of these fellows were quite a bit older than him, and they had never seen anybody with this kind of humor. It was…
That’s funny. Would you go and hear your dad play? Or were you . . . ?
